claims.text: The baseline system is zirconium-alloy cladding coated with a monolithic elemental Cr layer.
The proposed intervention is to incorporate approximately 3 at.% Al into the Cr coating by co-sputtering.
Co-sputtering can produce homogeneous incorporation of approximately 3 at.% Al in the Cr matrix.
Al in the modified Cr coating will segregate during high-temperature exposure.
The segregated Al will form a thin, continuous Al2O3-rich nanolayer at the Cr/Zr interface.
The Al2O3-rich interfacial nanolayer will be stable and adherent.
The Al2O3-rich interfacial nanolayer will reduce the kinetics of Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Adding approximately 3 at.% Al will maintain the inherent oxidation resistance of the Cr coating.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent premature coating failure.
The modified coating will exhibit significantly less interfacial element transport than the unmodified Cr coating.
The modified coating will sustain oxidation protection better than the unmodified Cr coating in normal subcritical water.
The modified coating will sustain oxidation protection better than the unmodified Cr coating in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of unmodified Cr coatings under high-temperature steam exposure.
The proposed modification is applicable in subcritical water at approximately 320°C and 11.3 MPa.
The proposed modification is applicable during short transient steam exposures up to approximately 1200°C.
The Al2O3-rich interfacial nanolayer is expected to remain stable across the stated normal-operation and accident-relevant regimes.
